message.content:
In this repository, I need to trace the full request path for a browser fetching another user's profile image (e.g. GET /users/:id/avatar or similar), from the HTTP handler down to the data layer / storage.

Please find:
1. The route/controller/handler that serves a user's profile image (search for terms like "avatar", "profile image", "profile_picture", "photo", etc. in routes and controllers).
2. Each function/method call hop between that handler and wherever the actual image bytes or file path are fetched (service layer, repository/DAO layer, storage abstraction, etc.).
3. The final data layer call — e.g., database query, S3/blob storage fetch, or filesystem read — that retrieves the stored image data.
4. Also note any authorization/permission checks encountered along the way (since this is "another user's" profile image, i.e. not the requester's own).

For each hop, give me: the symbol name (function/method/class) and the file path (with line number if easy to get).

Report back as a simple ordered list of hops with symbol and file path, from HTTP entry point to data storage layer. Be thorough — use grep/search across the whole repo, not just one directory, since this could be a monorepo with multiple services (web, api, backend, etc.).

I have the full picture now. Let me also verify the frontend piece briefly (UserAvatar component / img src) for completeness, and check `resolveBearer` quickly for the auth hop detail.

I now have a complete trace. Here's the full request path. ## Request path: `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar` This is the [usememos/memos](https://github.com/usememos/memos) repo (Go backend + React/TS web frontend). A user's avatar is not stored as a separate blob/file — it's stored as a base64 **data URI string** in the `user.avatar_url` column and streamed back on request. 1. **Route registration** — `FileServerService.RegisterRoutes` — `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125` Registers `fileGroup.GET("/users/:identifier/avatar", s.serveUserAvatar)` on the `/file` group. Wired up in `/bench/repo/server/server.go:81-82` (`fileserver.NewFileServerService(...)`; `.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)`). 2. **HTTP handler** — `(*FileServerService).serveUserAvatar` — `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168-207` Entry point for the request. 3. **Authorization/authentication check (hop within handler)** — `(*FileServerService).getCurrentUser` → `Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser` — `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:708-712` calling `/bench/repo/server/auth/authenticator.go:190-208` - Only invoked if `!s.Profile.AllowAnonymous()` (i.e., private instance with no `InstanceURL` set — `/bench/repo/internal/profile/profile.go:46-48`). - `AuthenticateToUser` → `resolveBearer` (`/bench/repo/server/auth/authenticator.go:149-174`, checks Access Token V2 or PAT) → falls back to `AuthenticateByRefreshToken` from cookie. - **Important finding**: this only verifies the requester is *some* authenticated user (or, on a public instance, allows anonymous access entirely). There is **no ownership/authorization check** that the viewer is the same user as `:identifier` — any logged-in (or, if public, any anonymous) caller can fetch any other user's avatar by username. 4. **Identifier resolution / user lookup** — `(*FileServerService).getUserByUsername` — `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715-717` Calls `s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{Username: &identifier})`. 5. **Store layer (cache-aside)** — `(*Store).GetUser` — `/bench/repo/store/user.go:148-169` Checks an in-memory `userCache` (only keyed by ID, so username lookups always miss it) then delegates to `(*Store).ListUsers`. 6. **Store layer** — `(*Store).ListUsers` — `/bench/repo/store/user.go:136-146` Delegates to the driver interface: `s.driver.ListUsers(ctx, find)`. 7. **DB driver (data layer)** — `(*sqlite.DB).ListUsers` (and equivalent `postgres.DB.ListUsers` / `mysql.DB.ListUsers`) — `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user.go:88-201` (analogous files: `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user.go`, `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user.go`) Builds and runs `SELECT id, username, role, email, nickname, password_hash, avatar_url, description, created_ts, updated_ts, row_status FROM user WHERE username = ? ...` — **this is the final data-layer call**, returning the `avatar_url` column (a data URI, e.g. `data:image/png;base64,...`) as part of the `store.User` row. 8. **Post-processing in the handler** — back in `serveUserAvatar` (`/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:192-207`): - `user.AvatarURL == ""` → 404 if no avatar set. - `(*FileServerService).parseDataURI` — `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737-...` — regex-parses the data URI into `imageType` + decoded `imageData` (base64 decode). - Validates `imageType` against `avatarAllowedTypes` (`/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:75-81`). - Sets security/cache headers and writes the bytes via `c.Blob(http.StatusOK, imageType, imageData)`. ### Notes / gaps found - Unlike attachments (`serveAttachmentFile`, same file, lines 130-163), which call `s.checkAttachmentPermission(ctx, c, attachment)` before serving the blob, **`serveUserAvatar` has no equivalent per-resource permission check** — it only gates on "is anyone authenticated" when the instance is private, not on relationship between viewer and the target user. So viewing "another user's" avatar is authorized by the mere fact of being logged in (or, on a public instance, without even that). - Actual avatar bytes are never read from S3/filesystem in this path — they live inline in the `user` table's `avatar_url` text column (contrast with attachments, which do support `LOCAL` filesystem, `S3`, and DB blob storage types — see `serveMediaStream`/`serveStaticFile` in the same file for that separate code path). - Frontend entry point that triggers this request: `/bench/repo/web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx` and `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:36` (`userpb.AvatarUrl = fmt.Sprintf("/file/%s/avatar", userpb.Name)`), which is what causes the browser's `` tag to hit this route for other users' profiles (e.g. on `/bench/repo/web/src/pages/UserProfile.tsx`).
